introduction.definition: A condensate recovery system returns hot condensate from steam users to the boiler. High-pressure condensate enters a flash vessel, where part of it flashes to low-pressure steam that is reused; the remaining condensate drains to a vented receiver, and duty/standby pumps return it to the boiler feed tank when the level switch calls.

pressure.title: Recover heat, water and chemicals
pressure.description: High-pressure condensate entering a lower pressure partly flashes to steam: flash fraction = (h_f,high − h_f,low) / h_fg,low (≈ 10–15 % from ~10 bar to atmosphere). The flash vessel sends this steam to the LP header; the remaining hot condensate (already treated water, ≈ 90–100 °C) returns to the boiler, saving fuel, make-up water and treatment chemicals. Pumps handling near-boiling water need generous NPSH, which is why the receiver is raised above them.

video_tutorials.title: Condensate Recovery System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Condensate Recovery System.
A condensate recovery system returns hot condensate from steam users to the boiler.

High-pressure condensate enters a flash vessel, where part of it flashes to low-pressure steam that is reused; the remaining condensate drains to a vented receiver, and duty/standby pumps return it to the boiler feed tank when the level switch calls.
Typical applications include process plants and boiler houses; heat-exchanger and tracer condensate collection.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Condensate Pump 1 (duty), Condensate Pump 1 (duty) — Shaft & Coupling (turning), Condensate Pump 2 (standby), Condensate Pump 2 (standby) — Shaft & Coupling (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Condensate Recovery System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Condensate Recovery System.
Check level, pump cycling and vent.
Inspect pump seals and check valves.
Inspect receiver internally.
Watch for pump cavitation: noise, low flow. Common cause: low NPSH (hot condensate, low head).
Watch for receiver overflow: hot water at overflow. Common cause: pump/float failure.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
